PROJECT ABSTRACT SUMMARYTHE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF A U.S. GEOLOGICAL SURVEY (USGS) FEDERALLY OWNED ENERGY AND MINERALS RESEARCH FACILITY (EMRF) IN GOLDEN, CO COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT BETWEEN THEUNITED STATES GEOLOGICAL SURVEY (USGS) AND COLORADO SCHOOL OF MINES.THE USGS GEOLOGY, GEOPHYSICS, AND GEOCHEMISTRY (G3) AND CENTRAL ENERGY RESOURCES (CER), SCIENCE CENTERS PROVIDE UNIQUE RESEARCH AND OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES IN CRITICAL MINERALS, ENERGY RESOURCE EVALUATION, AND OTHER ESSENTIAL ENERGY AND MINERAL PROGRAM PRIORITIES FOR THE USGS AND DOI.THROUGH THE BIPARTISAN INFRASTRUCTURE LAW (BIL), THE USGS WILL VASTLY EXPAND INVESTMENTS IN CRITICAL MINERALS RESEARCH, ADVANCE THE DATA PRESERVATION OF GEOLOGICAL AND GEOPHYSICAL DATA, AND SUPPORT CONSTRUCTION OF A NEW USGS RESEARCH FACILITY TO SUPPORT ENERGY AND MINERALS RESEARCH. THE USGS IS COMMITTED TO INVESTING IN OUR NATION'S INFRASTRUCTURE AND ADVANCING THE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE CLEAN ENERGY SUPPLY CHAIN. A NEW FACILITY WILL ENABLE COOPERATIVE SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH, EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT, AND TECHNOLOGICAL COLLABORATION TO MAXIMIZE CONTRIBUTIONS TO BASIC AND APPLIED EARTH SCIENCES FOR THE PURPOSE OF SOLVING NATURAL RESOURCE AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS, AND BENEFITTING LOCAL COMMUNITIES, GOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC OF COLORADO AND THE NATION.THE BIL PROVIDES $167 MILLION DIRECTLY TO THE USGS TO SUPPORT THE NEW ENERGY AND MINERALS RESEARCH FACILITY (EMRF). FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF A USGS-OWNED FACILITY TO SUPPORT ENERGY AND MINERALS RESEARCH AND APPURTENANT ASSOCIATE STRUCTURES, THROUGH A COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WITH AN ACADEMIC PARTNER. FUNDING IS PLANNED TO BE AVAILABLE IN FY 2022 UNTIL EXPENDED.ADDITIONAL FY 2023 AND FY 2024 FUNDING IS ANTICIPATED BY THE USGS INFRASTRUCTURE FIVE-YEAR PLAN TO COMPLETE THE PROJECT. ADDITIONAL FUNDING AMOUNTS WILL BE DETERMINED BY THE PROGRAM VALIDATION AND SCHEMATIC DESIGN TASK EFFORTS. USGS ENERGY AND MINERALS SCIENCE CAPABILITIES AND SPACE REQUIREMENTS WILL BE THE HIGHEST PRIORITY.THE U. S. GEOLOGICAL SURVEY INTENDS TO ESTABLISH A COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WITH THE COLORADO SCHOOL OF MINES (MINES) FOR THE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF A NEW FEDERALLY OWNED ENERGY AND MINERALS RESEARCH FACILITY (EMRF) TO BE LOCATED ON LAND OWNED BY MINES. THE NEW LABORATORY AND OFFICE FACILITY WILL SUPPORT USGS AND MINES ENERGY AND MINERAL SCIENCE OPERATIONS.PHASE 1 OF THE COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WILL FOCUS ON THE PROGRAM VALIDATION AND SCHEMATIC DESIGN ACTIVITIES OF THE PROJECT. PURSUANT TO THE REQUIREMENTS FOR A COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT, USGS WILL BE SUBSTANTIALLY INVOLVED THROUGHOUT PHASE 1 AND THE ENTIRE PROJECT ENSURING FEDERAL BUILDING REQUIREMENTS ARE INTEGRATED IN THE DESIGN AND THE NEW SPACE SUPPORTS USGS SCIENCE IN FURTHERANCE OF PROGRAMMATIC MISSION REQUIREMENTS.THE PROJECT SHALL BE LOCATED ON THE MINES CAMPUS WITH THE NEW FACILITY BEING ADJACENT TO THE EXISTING USGS GEOLOGIC HAZARDS SCIENCE CENTER.

PROJECT TITLE:  TIER-II MAGNETIC AND RADIOMETRIC DATA WITHIN THE WESTERN KUSKOKWIM RIVER (WKR) AIRBORNE GEOPHYSICAL DATA-ACQUISITION REGION FOR THE FFY2023 EARTH MRI PROGRAMPROJECT PERIOD:  07 01 2023 - 06 30 2025PURPOSE: THE RESULTING HIGH-QUALITY GEOPHYSICAL DATA WILL PROVIDE THE FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCING FUTURE DGGS AND USGS GEOLOGICAL MAPPING AND MINERAL-RESOURCE EVALUATIONS, AND HENCE, UNDERSTANDING OF THE AREA S CRITICAL-MINERAL POTENTIAL AS WELL. MAGNETIC DATA ARE USEFUL FOR DISTINGUISHING VARIOUS MAGNETIC UNITS AND FOR CORRELATING GEOLOGY THROUGH AREAS COVERED BY VEGETATION AND SURFICIAL DEPOSITS. INVERSIONS AND MODELLING OF AVAILABLE MAGNETIC AND ELECTROMAGNETIC DATA ARE USEFUL FOR BUILDING GEOLOGIC-MAP CROSSSECTIONS AND UNDERSTANDING THE 2D AND 3D GEOMETRY OF SUBSURFACE GEOLOGIC BODIES AND STRUCTURES.ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: THE DGGS WILL BE THE LEAD GEOLOGICAL SURVEY FOR GEOPHYSICAL-SURVEY CONTRACTING, DESIGN, QA QC, AND PUBLICATION. DGGS WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH THE USGS ON ALL ASPECTS OF GEOPHYSICAL-SURVEY DESIGN AND LOCATION. DGGS WILL CONTRACT DATA ACQUISITION TO PRE-QUALIFIED GEOPHYSICAL DATA-COLLECTION VENDORS THAT ARE ON OUR MASTER AGREEMENT LIST. INDIVIDUAL GEOPHYSICAL SURVEYS WILL BE AWARDED TO ONE OR MORE OF THESE VENDORS USING A COMPETITIVE-BID TASK ORDER SOLICITATION (TOS).DELIVERABLES AND OUTCOMES: WITHIN THREE YEARS OF RECEIPT OF FUNDING, ALL DATA FROM THE WKR AIRBORNE GEOPHYSICAL SURVEYS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC VIA THE DGGS WEB SITE IN DIGITAL FORMAT AFTER GOING THROUGH THE DGGS PUBLICATION-REVIEW AND APPROVAL PROCESS. DATA WILL BE PROVIDED IN A VARIETY OF INDUSTRY STANDARD FORMATS WITH CLEAR AND CONCISE METADATA AND README FILES.

PROJECT PERIOD: 3 4 24-3 3 25PROJECT TITLE: NEW TOOLS FOR FORECASTING AND MONITORING AGROCLIMATIC CONDITIONS IN THE DEVELOPING WORLDTHIS AWARD SEEKS TO IMPROVE THE MONITORING AND FORECASTING OF AGROCLIMATIC CONDITIONS IN FOOD INSECURE REGIONS OF THE DEVELOPING WORLD THROUGH FOUR DISTINCT ACTIVITIES: 1) AGROCLIMATIC MONITORING AND FORECASTING DATASETS AND TECHNIQUE DEVELOPMENT, 2) IDENTIFICATION OF HOMOGENEOUS CLIMATE ZONES, 3) INCORPORATION OF EXTREME TEMPERATURES AND EVAPORATIVE DEMAND IN MONITORING AND FORECASTING ACTIVITIES, AND 4) DEVELOPMENT OF CLIMATE SERVICES TO BETTER COMMUNICATE AGROCLIMATIC CONDITIONS TO STAKEHOLDERS. THE FIRST ACTIVITY CENTERS ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW MONITORING AND FORECASTING DATASETS AND METHODS TO SUPPORT DEEPER AND MORE PROACTIVE ANALYSIS OF AGROCLIMATIC CONDITIONS. KEY OBJECTIVES INCLUDE UPDATING AND IMPROVING TEMPERATURE AND PRECIPITATION DATASETS PRODUCED BY BLENDING SATELLITE AND IN SITU OBSERVATIONS WITH LONG-TERM AVERAGES. CURRENT PRODUCTS ARE WIDELY-USED AND ESSENTIAL TO MONITORING AND FORECASTING CONDITIONS, AND NEW, HIGH-QUALITY DATA STREAMS WILL INCREASE CAPABILITIES TO INTERROGATE PAST AND FUTURE DRIVERS OF MANY TYPES OF DROUGHTS.THE SECOND ACTIVITY SEEKS TO IDENTIFY HOMOGENEOUS CLIMATE REGIONS FOR THE CHARACTERIZATION OF RESPONSE TO VARIOUS CLIMATE DRIVERS. THIS WORK WILL IDENTIFY APPROPRIATE SCALES OF ANALYSIS AND FOCUS ON ANTICIPATED RESPONSES TO CLIMATE DRIVERS, BETTER SUPPORTING ENHANCED FORECAST ANALYSIS. UTILIZATION OF THESE REGIONS NOT ONLY ENHANCES THE ABILITY TO FORECAST VARIABLES LIKE PRECIPITATION AND TEMPERATURE, BUT CAN ALSO ASSIST IN FORECASTING AGRICULTURAL CONDITIONS BASED ON THE CLIMATE DRIVERS FOR A ZONE.THE THIRD ACTIVITY INVESTIGATES THE LINKAGES AND TRENDS BETWEEN EXTREME TEMPERATURES, HIGHER EVAPORATIVE DEMAND AND PRECIPITATION, AND THE CHANGES IN THAT RELATIONSHIP OVER TIME. IDENTIFYING THE ROLE OF EVAPORATIVE DEMAND IN CREATING OR EXACERBATING DROUGHT CONDITIONS CAN HELP IN ANTICIPATING, IDENTIFYING, AND QUANTIFYING POOR GROWING CONDITIONS, AS WELL AS THE RESULTING IMPACT ON CROP YIELDS OR PRODUCTION. RESOURCES WILL CAPITALIZE ON NEW DATA PRODUCTS FROM THE FIRST ACTIVITY, AS WELL AS EXISTING, PUBLICLY-AVAILABLE EVAPORATIVE DEMAND ESTIMATES. THE FINAL ACTIVITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IS RELATED TO DEVELOPING AND SUPPORTING CLIMATE SERVICES THROUGH THE TAILORING, TRANSMISSION, AND COMMUNICATION OF FINDINGS. THESE EFFORTS WILL TARGET BOTH ACADEMIC (CONFERENCE PROCEEDINGS AND PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS) AND NON-ACADEMIC SYSTEMS. THESE INCLUDE FAMINE EARLY WARNING SYSTEMS NETWORK (FEWS NET) REPORTING, SUPPORT TO OTHER RISK MANAGEMENT AND AGRICULTURAL ADVISORY AGENCIES, COOPERATION WITH METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENTS ON DATA AND CAPACITY BUILDING, AND THE IDENTIFICATION OF NEW PARTNERS THAT BRING INFORMATION TO SMALL-SCALE DECISION MAKERS, SUCH AS FARMERS AND WATER MANAGERS. THESE COMMUNICATION ACTIVITIES RAISE THE VISIBILITY AND INFLUENCE OF DATA PRODUCTS, GRAPHICAL PRODUCTS BASED ON THAT DATA, AND ANALYSES PRODUCED IN THE FIRST THREE ACTIVITIES.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT RANGE ACROSS A WIDE SPECTRUM OF USERS AND CONSUMERS. THIS WORK DIRECTLY SUPPORTS THE NEEDS OF FEWS NET BY PROVIDING AGROCLIMATIC DATASETS THAT WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO THEIR FOOD SECURITY OUTLOOK PROCESS. DATA PRODUCTS WILL BE AVAILABLE THROUGH THE UNITED STATES GEOLOGICAL SURVEYS EARLY WARNING WEB PORTAL AND OTHER PUBLIC REPOSITORIES. GOVERNMENT PARTNERS SUCH AS USGS, NASA, NOAA, AND USDA ACTIVELY USE CURRENTLY-PRODUCED OPERATIONAL DATA PRODUCTS, AND ANALYSES BASED ON THESE, TO DRIVE HYDROLOGIC AND AGRICULTURAL MODELS AND CONDUCT RESEARCH. FINALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL BENEFIT PARTNERSHIPS WITH STAKEHOLDERS THAT ADVISE AGRICULTURAL AND WATER RESOURCE DECISION-MAKERS IN THE FOCUS AREAS, SUCH AS NATIONAL METEOROLOGICAL AND AGRICULTURAL SERVICES AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS AND OUTLETS.

THERE ARE 425 THREATENED AND ENDANGERED PLANT SPECIES IN HAWAII, MANY POSSIBLY REQUIRING TRANSLOCATION FOR RECOVERY. PLANT TRANSLOCATIONS ARE EXPENSIVE, AND SPECIES OFTEN HAVE LIMITED TRANSLOCATION ATTEMPTS DUE TO THE AVAILABILITY OF SEEDS FOR PROPAGATION AND ASSOCIATED COSTS. IDENTIFYING LOCATIONS WHERE THE SPECIES ARE BEST SUITED AND PROTECTED FROM THREATS IS CRITICAL FOR INCREASING THE PROBABILITY OF SUCCESS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE MODELING FRAMEWORK FOR IDENTIFYING MICROSITES THROUGHOUT AND OUTSIDE OF A SPECIES  KNOWN RANGE THAT ARE MORE RESILIENT TO CHANGING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS, THEREBY INCREASING THE PROBABILITY OF TRANSLOCATION SUCCESS. USING SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION MODELS CURRENTLY UNDER DEVELOPMENT BY USFWS, CLIMATE SENSITIVITY MODELS WILL BE DEVELOPED BY USGS THROUGH HCSU TO DETERMINE HOW SENSITIVE EACH SPECIES IS TO ENVIRONMENTAL SHIFTS AND IDENTIFY RESILIENT MICROSITES ACROSS THE STATE. AFTER REVIEW OF THE MODELS, AT LEAST THREE SPECIES WILL BE SELECTED FOR EXPERIMENTAL OUTPLANTINGS TO TEST HOW WELL THE MODEL SELECTS SITES FAVORABLE TO SPECIES PERSISTENCE. THIS PROJECT WILL CREATE WEB-BASED DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS TO GUIDE FUTURE TRANSLOCATION EFFORTS FOR ALL LISTED PLANT SPECIES IN HAWAII, ULTIMATELY ENHANCING RECOVERY EFFORTS AND SUPPORTING MORE EFFICIENT USE OF LIMITED CONSERVATION RESOURCES.
